 UCF Men's Basketball off to an impressive start 
 UCF Men's Basketball off to an impressive start
 Sports 
 Knights outlast FGCU in overtime and rally past Yale 
 Today, 03:30 PM 
 Special to the Herald 
 Dior Johnson followed up a 41-point explosion against FGCU with a 28-points, 7-rebound against Yale, but it was Elijah Hulsewe (No. 19) who posted his first doubt-double of his UCF career with 10 points and 10 rebounds. 
 Author: Photos courtesy of UCFAA 
    ORLANDO — The UCF men’s basketball team opened up its regular season in fashion Monday night, outlasting FGCU, 96-95, in overtime inside Addition Financial Arena.
    “I thought we did a great job of showing our composure in the overtime securing a good win.” said Head Coach Johnny Dawkins, who improved to 10-1 in season-openers at home.
    Headlined by the return of Dior Johnson, the Knights (1-0) battled through a back-and-forth contest as the senior guard erupted for 41 points, going 13-of-15 from the floor, including 4-for-4 on 3-point attempts, setting the UCF Division I record for most points scored in a season opener and powering the Black and Gold to a thrilling home victory.
    The Knights' bench accounted for 42 of UCF's 96 points, led by Lewis Walker's 16 and Arturo Dean's 15. UCF held FGCU's bench scoreless until midway through the second half, limiting the Eagles' reserves to just 11 points for the game.
    The Knights held FGCU (0-1) to just one point off turnovers, improving upon their season-low mark of two allowed in 2025-26, recorded against VMI on Nov. 29 and No. 11 Texas Tech on Jan. 31.
    Johnson extended his streak of consecutive 20-point games to five and also marked his third career game with 40 or more points, while Walker extended his double-digit scoring streak to 14 games, ranking among just 39 current players with a streak of at least 14 consecutive games with 10-plus points.

 Knights rally past Yale 
    The Black and Gold turned up the pressure in the second half Friday night, powering past Yale, 87-75, inside Addition Financial Arena.
    Yale (1-1) built a lead of as many as 13 points, but the Knights (2-0), once again behind Dior Johnson (19 first half points), caught fire and cut the deficit to just three points, 42-39, at intermission.
    “A big part of any team’s success is finding way to win when things aren’t going as well,” said Head Coach Johnny Dawkins. “We’ve shown ability to do that in our first couple of games. We’ve been down at halftime and we fought hard to find a way to win.”
    The Black and Gold came out swinging after halftime. A turnover gave UCF an early opportunity, and Arturo Dean converted at the free-throw line. John Bol followed with a dunk to give the Knights their first lead of the night, 43-42. A pair of layups from Arturo Dean and Walker helped UCF build its momentum.
    Johnson continued to light up the scoreboard, draining a 3-pointer to extend his streak to six consecutive games with at least 20 points (he finished with a game-high 28 and also pulled down a career-high seven rebounds).
    The Bulldogs briefly evened the score at the 14:14 mark, but Walker answered with a layup to put the Knights back in front. Riley Kugel then took charge, stringing together seven points to help UCF carry a 61-59 advantage into the final 10 minutes.
    Isaiah Malone made his presence felt on both ends of the floor, recording a block at 8:49 before Johnson capitalized with a 3-pointer. Malone followed with a triple of his own, fueling a decisive run that pushed the Knights' advantage to 74-61.
    Kugel came up with a steal to spark another transition opportunity, setting up Arturo Dean for a layup as UCF continued to pull away.
    With the game in hand, Elijah Hulsewe added one final layup with a minute remaining to complete his first double-double as a Knight, finishing with 10 points and 10 rebounds.
    The Black and Gold showed great offensive teamwork in the second half with seven players netting at least two field goals each.
    UCF also committed just two turnovers throughout the contest, the fewest in the Johnny Dawkins era, and held the Bulldogs to zero points off turnovers, improving upon their season-low mark of one established in the season-opener against FGCU.

    Up Next: 
    The Knights will remain at home for three games this week, hosting South Alabama on Tuesday and then a pair of women’s/men’s doubleheaders against Georgia Southern at 8 p.m. on Friday and next Tuesday against Mississippi State at 7 p.m. The games will be streamed on ESPN+.
